lane: voice (his voice, many wordings, plain colours)

features.name: My voice (teach Ghosty your voice)
features.does: You read three sentences once; the phone learns your voice and keeps it on this phone only.
features.note: Better with the voice pack fetched on your tap; works without it.

features.name: People I've introduced
features.where: SETTINGS → VOICE & HOME → PEOPLE I'VE INTRODUCED
features.does: Someone you introduce says yes aloud and reads three sentences; Ghosty then knows their voice by name.

features.name: Who's talking, on the talk bar
features.where: Home → talk bar, after you speak
features.does: After each spoken turn the bar shows YOU, a name, NOT SURE WHO or A VOICE I DON'T KNOW; an unknown voice is held with GO ON / NOT NOW, and IT'S FINE FOR AN HOUR stops the asking.

features.name: The chat knows it's you
features.does: Every turn tells the brain what the phone really heard (you, not sure, a stranger, typed, or not taught yet), so it answers truly and never says it can't recognise you.
features.note: Telegram voice notes aren't scored: the phone isn't there to hear them.

features.name: Never a lock
features.does: Your voice never opens, pays or approves anything; the tap always does.

features.name: Many wordings, one meaning
say: Give us a shout in ten minutes
features.does: Plain, slangy and British ways of asking reach the right ability: radio, water, lights, timers, map, Lens, comic, documents, sheets, slides, photos, videos, arcade, board games, weather, news, settings, the look, agenda, money, library, learn.
features.note: Proven on 2,282 wordings. Telegram still relies on the brain's own word match for music.

features.name: Asks when it's one of two
features.does: One short question with both answers as keys (music or a game; room lights or a dark screen; white light or a white page); nothing happens until you tap.

features.name: Play music → the radio
features.does: Plays your last station or first favourite; with none, opens Radio to pick one; stops it on request.
features.note: A genre or a station by name ("play some jazz") goes to the brain.

features.name: Colours named plainly
features.where: SETTINGS → THEME, THE LOOK, SLIDES themes
features.does: Twelve colours shown as Blue, Grey, Orange, Yellow, Red, Purple, Green, Light blue, Pink, Lime, Peach, White; old names and synonyms (crimson, navy, emerald, teal…) all work, and the reply says what changed.
features.note: Game studio sprite colours (Night, Moss…) keep scene names.

features.name: The look by words
features.does: Grounds, looks, switches and colours changed by words on the phone with no AI; "change the colour" opens THE LOOK and says how to pick one.

upward.why: When he says something new and then taps the screen he meant, Ghosty offers to remember that wording, so next time it just works.
upward.builds_on: Many wordings layer + the two-way question keys

upward.idea: Wordings for every screen, not just the top 26
upward.why: Every room in the app answers in more than one wording, as the final round asked.

upward.idea: Numbers and amounts in any wording
upward.why: "Log half a litre", "two glasses", "a quarter of an hour" are understood exactly, not rounded.
upward.builds_on: The timer and water readers in the meanings layer

upward.idea: Voice that keeps up as he changes
upward.why: His voice print refreshes itself gently from turns it is sure of (cold, tired, outside), so NOT SURE WHO comes up less.
upward.builds_on: Voice print, the voice pack judge

upward.why: "Too short", "too noisy" or "sounded like two people", in plain words, so he knows to say a full sentence.
"Make it the colour of my car" or a colour picked from a photo becomes a thirteenth colour, named plainly ("dark teal").
"A bit darker red", "softer blue", "brighter" nudge the colour, and the reply names the new shade.
upward.builds_on: Colour names + the look by words

upward.idea: Colour for the room he's in
upward.why: "Make the money screen green" keeps one colour per room, still named plainly.

upward.idea: Undo by words for the look
upward.why: "Put it back" or "the one before" returns the last colour or look.

upward.idea: Meanings in every language he speaks
upward.why: "Pon música" or Urdu wordings reach the same abilities.
"Put some tunes on" from Telegram queues the radio for when he opens the phone, and the rest work there as they do in the app.
When he's recognised for sure at the start of the day, a one-line "Morning, it's you" with the Brief.

sideways.why: When a voice he introduced is talking, Ghosty keeps his private things (money, health, messages) out of the answer automatically.
Sam's timers, Sam's radio station, Sam's colour, chosen by the voice he introduced, never a stranger's.
Each screen lists three wordings that work on it, taken from the meanings table, so he never has to guess.
sideways.builds_on: Meanings table + the room you're in

sideways.why: Type or say anything vague and see the top three abilities it could mean, each a key.
Plain-named colours checked for contrast, with a "colour-blind safe" switch that picks distinguishable pairs.
"Make the lights red" uses the same plain names for his Home Assistant bulbs.
"When I say 'movie time', dim the lights and play nothing": his own phrases chained to abilities.
"Ghosty" said aloud starts listening, judged on the phone; still never a lock.

sideways.idea: Voice notes kept as his own
sideways.why: Short spoken notes saved with "by you" from the speaker tag, for the diary and memory.
"Calm colours" or "focus colours" pick a plain-named colour and look together.

cross.idea: Radio by meaning with favourites by name
cross.why: "Put on my morning station" plays the favourite he named.

cross.idea: Water and timers by any wording, said back as cards
cross.why: "Necked a pint" or "eggs for 6 minutes" lands on the right card at once.

cross.idea: Comic and slides colours by plain names
cross.why: "Make the speech bubbles red" or "slides in navy" use the same colour words.
"What's this thing?" or "have a look at this" opens the one point-and-know lens, already in the right mode.
"What did Sam ask you yesterday?" uses the speaker tag on remembered turns (only people he introduced).
A voice it doesn't know asking for money or messages gets the scam check line automatically.
